description:
Meet the Team Behind  A Little Hero _NEILO    

We are an interdisciplinary team combining expertise in Physical Therapy, Petroleum Engineering, Agricultural Engineering, Remote Sensing & GIS, Web Development, and Video Editing. Together, we bring scientific, engineering, and creative perspectives to NEILO, transforming space exploration challenges into an interactive educational experience that inspires young minds and promotes sustainable human life beyond Earth.
summary: Welcome to A Little Hero! Meet NEILO, an Egyptian child from the land of the Nile, who helps children around the world become the heroes of a mission to sustain life on Mars. We developed an interactive, personalized learning experience for children aged 7–12. Each child leads the mission, and the journey is designed to adapt to their choices. Guided by NEILO and characters inspired by our team’s backgrounds in agricultural engineering, petroleum engineering, medicine, and AI, children face challenges involving water, energy, food, crew health, communication with Earth, and protecting the crew from radiation. NASA data helps reveal the risks behind these challenges and brings them into the experience. More than a game, A Little Hero makes space exploration a hands-on learning experience that builds curiosity, problem-solving skills, and awareness of how to care for people and resources. Today’s children are tomorrow’s engineers and doctors, so helping them become informed and make responsible decisions is important for life on Earth and beyond.
details:
NEILO’s Project Solution

NEILO: First Signal is an educational adventure game designed for children approximately 7–12 years old. The game places the player inside an abandoned research base on Mars after a guidance problem separates the player’s capsule from the main crew.

With the help of NEILO, a small companion robot, the player must restore the base and make important decisions about energy, water, agriculture, and radiation. The game turns Mars science into interactive missions instead of presenting it as a simple slideshow.

The player begins by exploring the Arrival Bay, following the glowing objective, and finding NEILO. After that, the player completes four main missions that are connected to one another:

Agriculture: Choose and grow food for the crew.

Power Generation and Engine Activation: Repair the water-pump circuit.

Radiation Discovery: Study Curiosity/RAD measurements and repair the relay.

Water Preparation: Prepare enough water for the waiting crew.

How Does Our Solution Work?

In the game, the player progresses through a sequence of missions. Each mission has a clear objective, a limited number of actions, and a visible result. The missions demonstrate that a Mars base depends on several connected systems.

Agriculture — Plan the First Fresh Food

The player enters the Garden Workshop and chooses between two crops that growing in suitable space conditions : lettuce and soybean. The selected seed packet must be dragged into the growing tray.

After planting, the player must:

Turn on the grow light.

Give the crop water.

Advance the growth simulation.

Wait for the crop to reach the correct growth stage.

Harvest the crop.

This mission teaches that agriculture on Mars requires planning. The player must consider crop type, growth time, water, light, harvesting, and the needs of the crew

Power Generation and Engine Activation — Give the Water Pump a Heartbeat

In this mission, the player repairs the water-pump circuit. The player must turn on the breaker and connect the two cables correctly:

Connect the amber output cable to the amber socket on the water pump.

Connect the blue return cable to the blue socket.

Close the circuit so power can reach the pump motor.

The game explains that power moves the motor, and the motor turns the pump. This gives the player a simple introduction to electrical circuits, motors, machines, and energy management.

The task teaches that energy is limited and that the player must decide which system should operate first.

Radiation Discovery — Study Mars Field Evidence

The player opens the Field Notes mission and studies evidence collected from Mars. The mission shows a Murray Buttes diagram and a graph connected to the Curiosity rover and the RAD instrument.

The player can see:

The Curiosity/RAD measurement graph.

The Mars surface location.

The date of the observation.

The absorbed dose-rate reading in µGy/hour.

The task called “Repair the relay”, which allows the crew to receive the field notes.

This mission teaches children how scientific data should be read. Every measurement needs a place, instrument, date, and unit. The game presents the radiation readings as scientific evidence, not as a human safety limit.

Water Preparation — Prepare Water for the Waiting Crew

The player must prepare water before informing the crew that the base is ready. The water unit is connected to the power system and used to prepare water packs.

One water cycle:

Uses 2 battery units.

Prepares 2 water packs.

Helps the player reach the goal of 5 prepared water packs.

The water mission teaches that life-support resources must be prepared before communication or exploration. The crew cannot depend on the base until essential water supplies are ready.

What Benefits Does It Have?

NEILO helps children understand how a Mars habitat works through direct interaction and problem solving.

The game provides several benefits:

It teaches systems thinking by connecting power, water, food, communication, and safety.

It develops planning skills through crop selection and growth timing.

It teaches children how to read scientific measurements and understand their limits.

It encourages decision-making because the player has limited energy and must complete tasks in the correct order.

It makes science more accessible through NEILO’s explanations and guidance.

What Do We Hope to Achieve?

We hope to make Mars exploration understandable, educational, and enjoyable. Players should learn that living on Mars would require much more than landing a spacecraft.

What Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, or Software Did You Use?

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Canvas and Web Audio
